title: Negation and `abs` of decimals round to 34 significant digits (SP-1)
verdict: `-x`, `abs(x)` past 34 digits: rounded silently, or a raise at 10³⁸ - 1
description: `-x` and `abs(x)` of a decimal with more than 34 significant digits round it half up to 34 digits, in both modes and on both paths: `-12345678901234567890123456789012345678` (a `DECIMAL(38,0)`) gives -12345678901234567890123456789012350000, and `abs` of it 12345678901234567890123456789012350000. `0 - x` is exact. At 10³⁸ - 1 the rounding reaches 10³⁸, which does not fit, so `-x` raises `NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` even with ANSI off.
`Decimal.unary_-` negates the Scala `BigDecimal`, whose default `MathContext` is `DECIMAL128` (34 digits). Upstream bug SP-1.
reference: `negate` and `abs` of decimals are exact, and never overflow (the negation of a `DECIMAL(p,s)` fits it). Spark is wrong past 34 digits; a writer spells `-x` as `0 - x` and `abs(x)` as `CASE WHEN x < 0 THEN 0 - x ELSE x END`.

evidence.note: `unary_-`: `Decimal(-decimalVal, precision, scale)` on a Scala `BigDecimal`; `abs` calls it

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
